A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same neural-decoding framework and Allen Brain Observatory experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite renaming and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original movie-reconstruction and drifting-gratings results, architecture and objective ablations, scaling experiments, neural-data analyses and curriculum simulations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds comparator evaluations, a random-subset control, statistical scaling analysis and measurements of parameter changes during transfer.

M1.justification: POYO-SSL is renamed POYO-CAP, but the selected Cre lines, thresholds, 50% temporal masking, joint reconstruction/classification objective and task-specific decoders remain unchanged. Equations 1–7 and Algorithm S2 are retained. The embedding-transfer information in v2 Appendix A is newly documented detail, not evidence of an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Allen Brain Observatory calcium recordings from 13 Cre lines for movie reconstruction and drifting-gratings decoding. V2 names Natural Movie One explicitly, but does not establish added stimulus coverage. The new controls use retained data and tasks; the revised split description concerns evaluation protocol.

E2.justification: V2 substantially expands the evaluated comparisons: Table 3 adds CEBRA encoder plus U-Net decoder and size-matched random-subset pretraining, while Appendix K adds a capacity-matched Transformer decoder. V1 discussed CEBRA without evaluating it. The from-scratch comparator is renamed 'Baseline: Train on All' with its scores retained; Neuro-BERT remains excluded.

E3.justification: V1 Section 3.1 states that animals, sessions and neuron IDs are disjoint across all splits. V2 instead specifies downstream trial splits within sessions, allowing shared animals, with animal separation between pretraining and finetuning. This substantially revises the reported protocol without establishing that experiments were rerun. New comparisons also introduce size/capacity controls, and Figure 2 uses an expanded field of view.

E4.justification: V2 adds a random-subset ablation testing targeted selection against arbitrary selection, a Transformer-versus-U-Net decoder comparison, and encoder/readout weight-change analysis examining transfer mechanisms. It also assesses landscape roughness over an expanded field of view. These substantially extend the analyses; the existing encoder-freezing study and curriculum simulations are retained under renumbered appendices.

E5.justification: V2 adds 95% confidence intervals to the Fisher Information estimates in Table 2 and a 10,000-resample bootstrap regression with scaling slopes and p-values in Section 4.3/Figure 5. Table 3 already reported three-seed confidence intervals and paired tests in v1. No increase in training-run counts is established.

E6.justification: The headline SSIM 0.593 and DG accuracy 0.555, along with existing Table 3 scores, are retained. V2 adds CEBRA SSIM 0.481, random-subset SSIM 0.532/DG accuracy 0.254, Transformer-decoder SSIM approximately 0.48, encoder weight change 0.183% and readout-bias growth 12.4×. New scaling estimates further extend the findings. Landscape roughness changes from 2.41/878.24 to 14.8546/2048.4712 under the expanded field of view, rather than under identical conditions.

T1.justification: The loss equations, Fisher Information approximation, effective-size concept, composite efficiency score and mathematical content of the existing appendices are retained. Renaming 'Theoretical Analysis' to 'Numerical Analysis' does not alter the mathematics. The new transfer discussion supplies empirical measurements and interpretations, not a new theorem, proof or derivation.

C1.justification: V2 retains the three contribution bullets and headline decoding/scaling claims, but substantially narrows their framing. It explicitly presents hybrid pretraining, removes the conclusion's highest-reported-SSIM claim, and replaces the assertion that this selection strategy is necessary for scalable neural foundation models with a testable curriculum principle demonstrated under controlled mouse-visual-cortex conditions.

C2.justification: V1 interprets reconstruction examples as evidence against frame memorization. V2 acknowledges shared training/test stimulus sets and limits the interpretation to neural-to-frame mapping generalization, excluding entirely novel-stimulus reconstruction. It also qualifies the biological statistics as noncausal proxies and adds substantive explanations involving a stable encoder scaffold, adapting readouts and the decoder's spatial inductive bias.

D1.justification: New Appendix A supplies movie and gratings split proportions, shuffling choices, animal-overlap rules, unit-embedding initialization from N(0,0.02), encoder-only transfer and end-to-end finetuning details. Table 1 newly specifies statistics computed over full-recording ΔF/F traces. These disclosures materially improve reproducibility information; existing hardware, sample totals, loss weights and decoder specifications are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds a data-centric SSL paragraph distinguishing neuron/feature-source selection from sample pruning, citing Paul et al. (2021) and Zhuang et al. (2025). Garipov et al. (2018) and Neyshabur et al. (2020) support the new transfer interpretation. It also qualifies comparisons with fMRI research because modalities differ. The broader related-work coverage remains largely intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and conclusion are substantially rewritten, with additional revisions to the introduction, dataset description and supervision explanation. Terminology changes throughout from POYO-SSL to POYO-CAP and from SSL to pretraining in multiple headings. A transfer-analysis subsection, acknowledgements and three new appendices expand the structure, while existing appendix material is retained and renumbered.

P2.justification: Figure 1 updates input-trace examples and axes; Figure 2 redraws the landscapes over a wider range; Figure 5 adds markers, line styles and statistical legend entries. Table 3 gains two rows, and several displays move. These are localized display revisions: the reconstruction examples, representation plots and six supplementary figures are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the supervision requirements and tested generalization clearer, replacing misleadingly broad split and reconstruction descriptions with explicit limitations. Appendix A and the added comparator/control evidence improve assessability. The gains remain limited by strong mechanistic conclusions drawn from indirect weight and landscape measurements, and by the retained Table 2 contradiction between effective-size values and accompanying prose. Overall, transparency and evidential support improve.
